As of April 18, 2026, the winter wheat is already in the field here in Quzhou, so when I say “this year,” I mean my 2026 production year: finish the current wheat crop, plant summer maize right after wheat on the same land, and keep a smaller millet area as a safer, lower-input crop.

I have farmed a long time, and at my age I do not chase fancy schemes. I look at what my land has done, what water costs, and how much labor the family can really put in because some people are working off-farm. I will keep most of the land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is still my main income and the land is suited to it, but I will leave 6.4 mu in millet because millet is steadier in a dry or expensive-water year. On wheat, I will not cut fertilizer too hard because that can cost yield quickly, but I also will not over-irrigate because pumping from the well is expensive. For maize after wheat, the key is speed: harvest wheat, light tillage or direct seeding quickly, basal fertilizer down, then one topdress around jointing. Millet I manage more conservatively, with lower fertilizer and usually one irrigation at most if the rain is poor.
